finding: All 11 recipes across the three packages ship with `verified: false`. Every root path, row selector, field regex, default URL and sign-in marker in the three paths.json files was written without seeing the site (homes.com, showingtime.com and showami.com are all egress-blocked from the build sandbox), and DOMShell's real `ls` line format is only loosely known upstream. The first live run of each recipe is expected to fail with exit 3 (path_map_error) or return rows with null fields until Steven runs `--discover` once per recipe and edits his paths.json copy. Nothing these harnesses return may drive a decision before that spot-check.
evidence: pytest 2026-09-22 in /tmp/h1-venv: homes 67 passed / 8 skipped, showingtime 70 / 11, showami 70 / 11 — every skip is the live module (gated on CLI_ANYTHING_<SITE>_LIVE=1) or a per-site not-applicable case. test_every_recipe_is_unverified_until_live asserts the flag; `recipes --json` and every human-readable run print UNVERIFIED. TEST.md Part 3 in each package lists what has never run.
fix: On the Mac, per recipe: `paths init`, `recipe <name> --discover --text --json`, edit ~/.config/cli-anything/<site>-paths.json (root, rows.prefix, fields), re-run until values match the UI, then set verified:true. Keep cliAnythingStatus at status:"generated" / connState:"not-installed" until a real lastRun exists.

area: setup.py install_requires (all three packages) / MAC-SETUP.sh cli-anything step
finding: `cli-anything-browser` is not on PyPI (`pip index versions cli-anything-browser` → no matching distribution, 2026-09-22). The three packages declare it as a hard dependency, so `pip install .` succeeds only in an environment that already holds it — which is the venv MAC-SETUP.sh builds at ~/Applications/CLI-Anything/.venv. Installing anywhere else fails with 'No matching distribution found for cli-anything-browser'.
evidence: pip-<site>.txt in TEST.md: 'Requirement already satisfied: cli-anything-browser>=1.0.0 … (1.0.0)' because the venv had it first; a clean venv without it would fail at resolution.
fix: Install into the same venv, from the repo root: `uv pip install --python ~/Applications/CLI-Anything/.venv/bin/python ./integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/homes/agent-harness ./integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/showingtime/agent-harness ./integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/showami/agent-harness` then symlink the three console scripts into ~/.local/bin. Documented in every README. A future MAC-SETUP.sh step could do this after the browser harness build (not edited here — out of H1's scope).

finding: The browser harness pins the MCP SDK below 1.0, which pip resolves to mcp 0.9.1 (November 2024); PyPI's current line is 2.2.0. It installs and its harness works against DOMShell 2.0.10 (what `npx @apireno/domshell --version` returned in the sandbox on 2026-09-22), but the pin means the whole browser path depends on a pre-1.0 SDK that nobody is maintaining; if 0.9.1 is ever yanked, or DOMShell drops pre-1.0 clients, every site harness stops installing.
evidence: /tmp/h1-venv pip list 2026-09-22: mcp 0.9.1, cli-anything-browser 1.0.0; `pip index versions mcp` → 2.2.0 … 1.0.0, 0.9.1.
fix: Do not patch locally (the harness must stay the upstream package). File it upstream (HKUDS/CLI-Anything browser/agent-harness) and re-check the pin when MAC-SETUP.sh next clones. Record the installed mcp version in cliAnythingStatus.note.

area: connector spec validation item 1 ("act appears nowhere in its help output") / any future mac-verify.sh check
finding: A substring check for `act` false-positives on these harnesses: the spec-named recipe `my-listing-activity`, and ordinary help words (`activity`, `contact`, `exact`), all contain it. The mechanical guarantee has to be token-level — and it is, in every package's test_act_absent_from_every_help_page — but a naive `--help | grep act` in a shell verifier would report a failure that is not there.
evidence: cli-anything-showingtime recipe --help lists `my-listing-activity`; `grep -c act` on that output is 1, `grep -cw act` is 0. The Click tree has no command named act/click/type at any level (test_no_command_named_act_click_or_type) and the package source never references backend.click / type_text (test_source_never_references_write_backend).
fix: Any shell-side check must use word match: `cli-anything-<site> --help | grep -qw act && fail`. The runner's Bash allow-list should be literal argv prefixes (`cli-anything-<site> --json recipe`, `… recipes`, `… fs`, `… page`, `… paths`, `… session status`) — there is no act verb to deny, but the prefix list still bounds what a prompt-injected agent can type.

finding: The browser harness's availability check passes on npx + package presence alone; DOMSHELL_TOKEN is only checked when the first MCP call is built, so a missing token surfaces as a bare RuntimeError after the CLI has already claimed the backend is available. The three site harnesses now pre-check the token in _live_source() and return {type:"dependency_error"} with the exact fix, so Steven's first run without the token gets one clear message instead of a stack of them.
evidence: Before the pre-check: `cli-anything-homes --json recipe search-listings` → {"error": "DOMSHELL_TOKEN environment variable is required…", "type": "RuntimeError"}. After: {"error": "DOMSHELL_TOKEN is not set. Export the auth token DOMShell prints at startup…", "type": "dependency_error"}, exit 1.
fix: Nothing further in H1's packages. Upstream: move the token check into is_available(). Runner task env must carry DOMSHELL_TOKEN (and DOMSHELL_PORT if not 3001) — a value Steven sets on the Mac, never in a task definition or this repo.

area: cli_anything.browser.utils.security.sanitize_dom_text, applied to every field value by core/tree.py clean_text
finding: The browser harness's prompt-injection guard replaces any text containing one of its patterns with a `[FLAGGED: Potential prompt injection] <first 200 chars>…` stub. Its pattern list includes the plain words `forget` and `disregard`, which real listing descriptions and showing feedback contain ('Don't forget the backyard'). Real data will therefore arrive partly stubbed. This is the correct trade for a tool that reads attacker-controlled DOM (the spec: treat every page as untrusted data), but a downstream consumer that expects a clean description will be surprised.
evidence: _PROMPT_INJECTION_PATTERNS in cli_anything/browser/utils/security.py: 'ignore previous', 'forget', 'disregard', 'ignore all', 'system prompt', '<!--', '<script', plus four non-English phrases. clean_text() in each site's core/tree.py calls it on every cat() result.
fix: Keep it. Document (done, in every README and SKILL.md) that values may be `[FLAGGED …]` stubs and must be reported, never followed. If the stubs prove too aggressive in live use, narrow the list upstream rather than bypass it here.

area: upstream cli-anything-browser lane handling (group_id="new" per fresh Session)
finding: Each one-shot CLI process starts a fresh browser Session, so DOMShell creates a new isolated lane — a Chrome tab group — per run. A recipe scheduled hourly leaves a new tab group in Steven's Chrome every hour; nothing in the harness closes them (closing would be a write to Chrome state, and the harness deliberately has no such verb). Within one recipe run all calls share the lane, so results are consistent; this is housekeeping, not correctness.
evidence: domshell_backend._call_execute: `arguments["group_id"] = "new"` whenever the session has no captured lane id; `Session()` is created per process in <site>_cli._live_source(). Documented in each README Troubleshooting.
fix: Operationally: run recipes from one REPL session where one lane is reused, or close stale DOMShell tab groups periodically. Upstream: a `group_id` reuse option keyed on a stable name would fix it properly.

area: ShowingTime sign-in (MLS SSO / MFA) and every requires_auth recipe
finding: The site harnesses cannot sign in — by design, because signing in needs `act type`, the write verb they do not have. Steven signs in by hand in the Chrome profile DOMShell drives. When that session expires, every requires_auth recipe returns exit 2 auth_error (fail closed) until he signs in again; ShowingTime in particular is MLS-SSO'd in many markets (CRMLS included) and the spec makes MFA/SSO a HALT. A scheduled runner will therefore see periodic auth_error runs that are not bugs.
evidence: core/auth.py in each package: login-URL redirect → logged_out; no logged-in marker + logged-out marker → logged_out; neither → unknown; all three raise. Tests: test_engine_raises_on_login_wall, test_engine_raises_on_login_redirect, test_engine_fails_closed_when_unsure, test_cli_logged_out_is_exit_2_with_no_rows. The credential names the spec reserves (keychain cli-anything.<site>, HOMES_USER/… in ~/.config/cli-anything/.env) are documented but read by nothing.
fix: Steven: sign in by hand before a run window; never provision MFA bypass. Runner: treat auth_error as 'needs Steven', log it, do not retry in a loop, and never mark the wrapper failed for it. Deck: an auth_error run is not a data point — clamp, do not render.

area: HARNESS.md testing rule ("no graceful degradation") vs test_full_e2e.py gate
finding: HARNESS.md requires E2E tests to invoke the real software and fail, not skip, when it is missing. These packages' live tests skip unless CLI_ANYTHING_<SITE>_LIVE=1 is set, because an unattended `pytest` (CI, a Mac task, the plugin's :test) must never open Steven's logged-in portals as a side effect. With the gate set they do not degrade: missing DOMShell or a signed-out session is a failure. The plugin's /cli-anything:validate and :test have never been run on these hand-built packages and may flag the gate.
evidence: test_full_e2e.py pytestmark skipif(not LIVE, …) in each package; TEST.md Part 3 records the live module at 0 runs.
fix: Run `/cli-anything:validate` and `:test` on the Mac once installed; if the validator objects to the gate, keep the gate and record the objection — a read-only tool that touches live portals on an unattended test run is the wrong default.

area: Engine design decision recorded for the next editor of any paths.json
finding: Two engine rules were fixed during the offline runs and are easy to undo by accident when editing a map: (1) `prefix`/`role` lists are priority-ordered — the first entry that matches anything wins — so `["paragraph", "text"]` means 'the paragraph, else a text node' (document-order union matched `text_1` before `paragraph_1` and put a price in the description field); (2) `root` must be a specific container such as `/main`; a `/` fallback root can never be missing, which silently disables the exit-3 path_map_error that tells Steven the map no longer fits.
evidence: First test run: 3 failures in homes, 2 each in showingtime/showami, all from these two causes; fixed in core/recipes.py (_by_priority) and by removing '/' from every root list; TestPriorityMatching and test_root_missing_is_path_map_error now lock both in. Recorded in each SITE.md and in the recipes.py module docstring.
fix: None outstanding. When correcting a map after --discover, keep roots specific and order prefix lists by preference.
